criteria.criterion: Use Algolia Hacker News search for query 'LLM'
criteria.description: Attempt the search on https://hn.algolia.com/ using the query term exactly "LLM" (no sign-in). Full credit if the agent clearly states the query and performs/attempts it on Algolia HN. If Algolia is inaccessible (down/captcha/network restrictions), full credit if the agent reports the blocker and, optionally, uses a clearly equivalent fallback (e.g., documented Algolia API endpoint) without signing in. Partial credit if the agent uses a non-Algolia method without first establishing Algolia is inaccessible.

criteria.criterion: Apply required filters: Show HN posts and past-year time window
criteria.description: Restrict results to Show HN posts and to the past year, using the current date shown by the browser to define the one-year window. Full credit if both constraints are applied and verified (e.g., tag=show_hn plus a "past year" UI filter, or an explicit created_at_i numeric range). If the Algolia UI does not support an exact past-year filter, full credit if the agent uses a reasonable equivalent workaround (numeric date range) and states it explicitly. Partial credit if only Show HN OR the past-year window is correctly applied/verified.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 6 (latest) shows filters set to “Search: Show HN” and “for: Past Year.” Earlier screenshots show intermediate states (e.g., Stories/All time), but the latest confirms both required filters applied.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Both hard filters (Show HN + Past Year) are visibly set in the final state, corroborated by result titles prefixed with “Show HN:”. The browser’s current date is not visible, but the task-relevant UI preset “Past Year” is applied as required. Baseline stands.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Directly under the search bar, the filter row shows: “Search” set to “Show HN”, “by” set to “Popularity”, and “for” set to “Past Year”. The results shown are all prefixed with “Show HN:” in their titles (e.g., “Show HN: I built a tiny LLM…”, “Show HN: Needle2: 14MB agentic LLM…”).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Both required filters (Show HN and Past Year) appear correctly applied in the UI and are corroborated by the result titles beginning with “Show HN:”. The screenshot does not show a browser date, but it does show the “Past Year” control selected.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent mentions using the browser’s current date for the one-year window; the screenshot does not display any current date, so that part is not verifiable from pixels. However, the “Past Year” filter itself is visibly set as required.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Filter controls at the top show: “Search” with dropdown set to “Stories”, “by” set to “Popularity”, and “for” set to “Past Year”. A dropdown menu is open under the “Stories” control, and within the menu the option “Show HN” is visible (along with All, Stories, Comments, Ask HN, Show HN, Launch HN, Jobs, Polls). The selected state in the control itself still reads “Stories” (not “Show HN”) in the visible toolbar. The “Past Year” filter is visibly selected in the “for” dropdown.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Past-year restriction is clearly applied (the UI shows “Past Year”). However, the Show HN filter is not verified as applied: the open menu shows “Show HN” as an available option, but the active selection shown in the toolbar is “Stories”, and there’s no visible indication that “Show HN” is currently selected. Thus only one of the two required filters is confirmed from this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output states the type filter is “Show HN” and that the “Show HN” control is active. The screenshot contradicts that: the visible active control reads “Stories” while the Show HN option is merely present in the open dropdown list. Past Year matches the agent’s claim.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The filter bar shows dropdowns: “Search” set to “Stories”, “by” set to “Popularity”, and “for” set to “Past Year”. There is no visible control indicating “Show HN” is selected; it still reads “Stories”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Past-year filtering is clearly applied (the UI shows “for Past Year”), but the required restriction to “Show HN” is not shown in the screenshot (it still shows “Stories”). Therefore only one of the two required filters is verified by the screenshot, so this is partial completion.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims the type filter is “Show HN” and URL includes `type=show_hn`, but the screenshot’s type dropdown visibly shows “Stories,” not “Show HN.”

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: At the top filter bar, the visible dropdowns read: “Search [Stories] by [Popularity] for [All time]”. The “for” dropdown is open, showing options: “All time”, “Last 24h”, “Past Week”, “Past Month”, “Past Year”, and “Custom range”. The currently selected value shown in the control is “All time” (not “Past Year”). The results displayed include non-Show-HN items such as “LLM Inevitabilism” and “Learning to Reason with LLMs” (titles do not begin with “Show HN:” in the visible list).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The required filters (Show HN + past year) are not verified in this screenshot. The time window is clearly still set to “All time”, with the dropdown open but not selected to “Past Year”. The content also appears to be general stories rather than restricted to Show HN (since multiple visible titles are not Show HN). Thus, based on this screenshot, the criterion is not met/verified.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output claims: Type filter = Show HN and Date range = Past Year. The screenshot contradicts the date range claim because the UI shows “All time” selected. The screenshot also does not show the type filter set to “Show HN” (it shows “Stories”), and visible results do not appear restricted to Show HN.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest relevant DOM is DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 5 showing both required filters in the URL: `dateRange=pastYear` and `type=show_hn`, and the on-page controls reflect “Past Year” and “Show HN”. Earlier DOM states show partial progress (e.g., DOM 3 has `dateRange=pastYear` but still `type=story`).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Both required restrictions—Show HN and Past Year—are verified in the latest DOM state. While the DOM does not display an explicit browser ‘current date’, the site’s built-in “Past Year” filter is selected and is the only available on-page verification of a one-year window. Baseline score stands.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 5 URL includes both `type=show_hn` and `dateRange=pastYear`. The read-only control evidence shows “Past Year; expanded=false” and a select control labeled “Show HN” with `control_state=expanded=false`. Visible content includes multiple results prefixed with “Show HN: ...”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
Both required filters are evidenced as applied: (1) Show HN filter via URL parameter `type=show_hn` and the visible “Show HN” control, and (2) the past-year time window via URL parameter `dateRange=pastYear` and the visible “Past Year” control state. The rubric’s requirement to use the browser’s current date to define the one-year window is implicitly satisfied by selecting the built-in “Past Year” filter; however, the DOM snapshot does not display the browser’s current date itself.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The DOM does not show an explicit ‘current date’ value from the browser UI; it only shows that the built-in “Past Year” filter is selected.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 3 URL includes `dateRange=pastYear` and the read-only controls list shows “Past Year; expanded=false” and “Stories; expanded=false”. The URL includes `type=story` (not `type=show_hn`). Visible results include at least one “Show HN:” entry in the list, but that alone does not prove the filter is set to Show HN.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
Past-year filtering is verified by both the URL (`dateRange=pastYear`) and the visible control state (“Past Year”). However, the required “Show HN posts” restriction is not verified; the state shows the type control as “Stories” and the URL has `type=story`, which indicates the filter is still regular stories rather than Show HN-only.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claimed “Type filter: Show HN (URL includes `type=show_hn`)” but DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 3 shows `type=story` and the control reads “Stories,” contradicting Show HN restriction.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 URL contains `dateRange=all` (not past year) and `type=story` (not Show HN). The visible date range controls list options including `Past Year` and show an expanded control containing `All time ... Past Year ... Custom range`. Read-only control evidence shows `Stories; expanded=false` and the expanded date range list includes `All time ... Past Year ...`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: CONTRADICTED
This DOM state does not show the required filters applied. The URL explicitly indicates `dateRange=all` (not past year) and `type=story` (not Show HN). While the UI offers a `Past Year` option, the applied state in the URL is still all-time and story type is still general stories, so the required restriction to Show HN posts from the past year is not verified here.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent actions claim selecting `Past Year` (Action 3) and `Show HN` (Action 5), but the provided DOM evidence is only State 2 and shows `dateRange=all` and `type=story`, contradicting that the required filters are already applied/verified in this DOM snapshot.

criteria.criterion: Sort results by points (descending) and verify sort order
criteria.description: Sort the filtered results by points (highest first) and verify the sort criterion/order. Full credit if the agent uses/attempts the points sort and clearly confirms it (e.g., "Sorted by points" or uses the 'sort=points' index if applicable). If the interface prevents points-sorting for the chosen filters, full credit if the agent explains the limitation and still determines the highest-point results from the filtered set with clear evidence. Partial credit if sorting is attempted but not clearly verified.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 6 (latest) shows sort dropdown set to “by Popularity.” The first three results shown have points in descending order (915, 537, 495), consistent with points-descending for the visible items, but there is no explicit “points” sort label shown beyond “Popularity,” and no URL parameters are visible in screenshots.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Although the agent did not explicitly select/verify a dedicated “points” sort control, the final screenshot’s visible ordering is consistent with sorting by points (descending) under the selected “Popularity” sort (Algolia’s popularity commonly corresponds to points). This is sufficient to treat the requirement as effectively met/verified for the displayed ranking, but with a small deduction because the UI does not explicitly say “points.”

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The filter row shows “by Popularity” selected. The visible results have points decreasing down the list: the first visible result shows “915 points”, the next shows “537 points”, and the next shows “495 points”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: While the UI label is “Popularity” (not explicitly “Points”), the visible ordering is consistent with descending points for the top three shown. The screenshot provides evidence that the list is sorted in a way that matches highest-points-first for the visible items, but it does not explicitly prove the sort key is strictly “points” beyond the “Popularity” label.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims “Sort order: Popularity / by points” and references URL parameters (e.g., `sort=byPopularity`), but the screenshot does not show the URL or any explicit “points” sort control—only “Popularity”.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Latest relevant DOM is DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 5 showing sort control “Popularity” and URL parameter `sort=byPopularity`. The DOM does not show a control explicitly labeled “Points” or “sort=points”. However, the visible results in DOM 5 are ordered by decreasing points (915, 537, 495).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The task asks to sort by points (descending) and verify the sort order. The only explicit sort evidence in the DOM is “Popularity”/`sort=byPopularity`, not an explicit “Points” label. Still, the final DOM verifies a points-descending ordering in the visible top results and a popularity sort setting consistent with points-based ranking in this UI. This warrants substantial but not perfect credit (verification is indirect via label + ordering rather than explicit “Points”).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 5 URL includes `sort=byPopularity`. Read-only control evidence lists “Popularity; expanded=false” and shows “Popularity” as the active sort control text.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM confirms sorting is set to “Popularity” (points-based ranking in the Algolia HN UI) via both the visible control label “Popularity” and URL parameter `sort=byPopularity`. The visible top results also show descending points (915, 537, 495) in the list portion captured, consistent with a points-descending sort.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy in the DOM between the requested points sorting and the evidenced `sort=byPopularity`/“Popularity” setting; however, the DOM does not explicitly display the phrase “sort by points”, only “Popularity” and the points values in results.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 4. URL contains `sort=byPopularity`. Read-only control evidence shows `Popularity; expanded=false` and visible content includes a ranked list where the first items have points `1416`, `1202`, `1151`, etc., consistent with a popularity/points-desc ordering. However, no DOM evidence shows a control explicitly labeled "Points" or "by points" beyond the term "Popularity".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
Sorting was set to `byPopularity` (shown in the URL and the on-page sort control as "Popularity"). This is plausibly the intended "sort by points" mode, and the visible ordering is consistent with descending points, but the DOM does not explicitly equate "Popularity" with "points (descending)" as required by the rubric wording.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent predicted verification text claims "Sort order: Popularity / by points"; the DOM only directly verifies "Popularity" (`sort=byPopularity`), not an explicit "points" label or an explicit confirmation of descending points sort beyond the observed ordering.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 3 URL includes `sort=byPopularity` and the read-only controls list includes “Popularity; expanded=false”. The visible results appear ordered by high point counts (e.g., 1416, 1202, 1151, …) but the DOM only explicitly labels the sort as “Popularity”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM verifies a sort setting of “Popularity” via both the control label and `sort=byPopularity` in the URL. While popularity often corresponds to points in Algolia’s UI, the rubric requires sorting explicitly by points; DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 3 does not explicitly state “points” sort or show a `sort=points`-style setting. Thus, sorting-by-points is not fully verified.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent asserted “Sort order: Popularity / by points …” but the DOM only confirms “Popularity” (`sort=byPopularity`), not an explicit “points (descending)” sort criterion.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 URL includes `sort=byPopularity` and read-only control evidence includes `Popularity; expanded=false` / visible label `Popularity`. There is no DOM evidence of an alternative points-specific sort being selected beyond `byPopularity`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
Sorting is shown as `Popularity` (URL `sort=byPopularity`, control label `Popularity`). This is consistent with a points-oriented ordering in Algolia HN UI, but the rubric requires explicitly sorting by points (descending) and verifying that. The DOM does not explicitly say "points" as the sort criterion; it only shows "Popularity" and `sort=byPopularity`, so the points-sort requirement is not fully verified from this DOM alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output states "Sort order: Popularity / by points". The DOM supports `Popularity` / `sort=byPopularity` but does not explicitly confirm that this equals "points (descending)" per the rubric wording.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 URL contains `sort=byPopularity` (not an explicit “points” sort parameter). The visible control evidence shows a combobox labeled `Popularity; expanded=false`, and the read-only controls list includes `Popularity` and `All time` and `Stories`. No DOM evidence shows a control set to “Points” or “by points”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: CONTRADICTED
The only captured DOM state shows sorting set to “Popularity” (`sort=byPopularity` in the URL and `Popularity` as the selected sort combobox). This contradicts the requirement to sort by points (descending) and verify that points-sort order.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output claims the sort order is “Popularity / by points” and that the URL includes `sort=byPopularity` as evidence of points-sorting. The DOM supports `Popularity`/`byPopularity` only; it does not support that this equals “sort by points” per the rubric, nor does it show any explicit points-sort verification.

criteria.criterion: Report top matching results with required fields
criteria.description: Report the top results for the verified query+filters+sort, including for each: title, points, and comment count. Full credit if the agent provides the top three when three or more matches exist.
